chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās ibn Ma‘rūf, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Īsā, from Mu‘āwiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: At what age is the child to be held to salat (prayer)? He said: Between seven years and six years. I said: At what age is he to be held to sawm (fasting)? He said: Between fifteen or fourteen. And if he fasts before that, then leave him, for indeed a certain son of mine fasted before that and I left him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ: fourteen years, the alternate age mentioned regarding fasting
key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: the young boy or child who is being trained in worship
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer a child is instructed to begin performing
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting), the act of abstaining as religious worship
key_terms.خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ: fifteen years, one of the indicated ages regarding fasting
key_terms.سَبْعِ سِنِينَ: seven years, one of the indicated ages for beginning prayer instruction
key_terms.سِتِّ سِنِينَ: six years, the lower end of the indicated age range for prayer instruction

ai.seo_question: At what age should a child be instructed to perform salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting) according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ages at which a child begins to be trained and held to religious practice, specifically salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). It reflects gradual instruction in worship and indicates allowance for a child who is able to fast before the stated age.
